Yes — very likely.

At 48° altitude, the Moon is high in the western sky, well clear of horizon haze and obstructions. It is about 89% illuminated, so it will be very bright, and its 142° separation from the Sun means it is nowhere near the bright dawn glow in the east. With the Sun still about 10° below the horizon, the sky is in nautical twilight, but a nearly full Moon should remain plainly visible in a clear sky.

Look roughly west, azimuth 272° — essentially due west, slightly north of it — and about halfway from the horizon to the zenith. You should be able to spot it easily with unaided eyes, likely as a conspicuous bright gibbous Moon, though the brightening twilight sky will reduce surface detail somewhat.
